data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
data.summary: Scientists have discovered chemically confirmed traces of ancient blood inside 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones, challenging assumptions about how long biological molecules can survive. The extraordinary preservation could unlock new clues about dinosaur physiology and even help scientists search for ancient life elsewhere in the universe.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years

data.title: ScienceDaily: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins
data.summary: A study of nearly 5,800 adults found that heart scans measuring calcium buildup in the arteries led to the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events as traditional risk assessments, despite recommending statins to far fewer patients. Surprisingly, patients advised to take statins based on their scans were nearly three times as likely to stick with their medication, raising intriguing questions about how doctors should identify and treat heart disease risk.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

data.summary: November's night sky is packed with celestial wonders, from bright meteor fireballs and a close pairing of Mars and Jupiter to a spectacular supermoon. Meanwhile, NASA's Voyager 1 is making history by becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth.

data.title: ScienceDaily: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space
data.summary: After nearly 22 years of exploring the universe’s most violent explosions, NASA’s Swift Observatory has re-entered Earth’s atmosphere over Indonesia. Originally designed to last just two years, the pioneering space telescope transformed our understanding of black holes, exploding stars, and mysterious cosmic outbursts.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space

data.title: ScienceDaily: For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
data.summary: Full-fat dairy may not be the health villain it has long been portrayed as, according to a new study finding that three daily servings did not worsen weight, cholesterol, or insulin resistance over 12 weeks. Researchers also observed improvements in blood pressure and nutrient intake, raising questions about longstanding recommendations to choose low-fat dairy.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise

data.title: ScienceDaily: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
data.summary: A surprising new study suggests that an anti-aging drug could help protect people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease. Researchers found that just four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant, with women showing the strongest benefits. Because declining blood flow can occur years before Alzheimer's symptoms appear, the discovery raises hopes for preventing or delaying the disease before memory loss begins.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin

data.summary: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive
data.summary: Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually just by turning food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades largely driven by population growth. Unlike fossil fuel emissions, however, the CO2 we exhale is part of the natural carbon cycle, and scientists say measuring it more accurately could improve climate models.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
data.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined

data.title: ScienceDaily: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
data.summary: A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly, they identified a way to trigger this brain rewiring without the behavioral response associated with psychedelic effects.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect

data.title: ScienceDaily: A 24-hour fast triggers a surprising repair response in the gut
data.summary: Scientists have discovered that fasting for just 24 hours increases a beneficial gut bacterium that helps the intestines regenerate after radiation damage. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A 24-hour fast triggers a surprising repair response in the gut

data.title: ScienceDaily: MIT scientists turn immune cells into cancer killers inside the body

The breakthrough could make powerful immune therapies dramatically simpler and less expensive while opening new possibilities for treating cancer and autoimmune diseases.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: MIT scientists turn immune cells into cancer killers inside the body

data.title: ScienceDaily: A nuclear blast could save Earth from an asteroid, but there's a catch
data.summary: A nuclear explosion might save Earth from a deadly asteroid, but new research suggests that hitting the wrong side could make the difference between success and disaster. Scientists found that an asteroid's irregular shape can dramatically affect how it responds to an X-ray blast, with deflection effectiveness varying nearly fivefold depending on the angle.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A nuclear blast could save Earth from an asteroid, but there's a catch

data.title: ScienceDaily: Ancient Siberian tomb reveals surprising secrets of cannabis use 2,800 years ago
data.summary: Scientists investigating a 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb discovered roughly 1,000 cannabis seeds and chemical evidence suggesting ancient Scythians used the plant for its intoxicating effects. data.title: ScienceDaily: Stronger flu shot linked to nearly 55% lower Alzheimer's risk
data.summary: A surprising new study suggests that a stronger flu shot could offer older adults significantly greater protection against Alzheimer's disease. data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover a hidden warning sign of cannabis addiction

data.title: ScienceDaily: A little-known protein could be a major culprit in type 2 diabetes
data.summary: Scientists have discovered that a buildup of a protein called Miro1 may be a hidden driver of insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes, with preclinical experiments showing that removing it restores the muscles’ response to insulin. data.title: ScienceDaily: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
data.summary: Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” plays a surprisingly important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean. Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected connection between ocean slime and Earth's climate.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered
data.summary: Researchers have discovered a stunning new species of tiny orange-patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon, but its survival may already be at risk. Named Laimosemion laranja, the brilliantly colored killifish measures less than three centimeters long and was found in just three small forest pools. Its extremely limited habitat is threatened by mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists wipe out deadly brain tumors in every mouse tested with new cancer therapy

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
data.summary: Scientists have uncovered fossils of a giant rodent that lived in Thailand 34 million years ago, revealing that enormous rodents evolved much earlier than previously thought. Named Yakamys sirindhornae, the ancient animal may have weighed around 66 pounds, roughly twice as much as other known rodents of its time.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago

data.title: ScienceDaily: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
data.summary: A bizarre, heavily armored amphibian roamed the oceans 237 million years ago, despite the fact that modern amphibians cannot survive entirely in saltwater. Discovered in China, the giant salamander-sized creature may be the first known amphibian to have adapted to a fully marine existence.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian

data.title: ScienceDaily: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
data.summary: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images

data.title: ScienceDaily: Eating less protein could slow aging, review of 350 studies finds
data.summary: A major review of more than 350 studies suggests that eating less protein could slow aging, improve metabolic health, and potentially extend lifespan, challenging the widespread belief that more protein is always better. Researchers warn that many sedentary adults may be consuming too much protein, while emphasizing that individual needs depend on age and physical activity.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Eating less protein could slow aging, review of 350 studies finds

data.title: ScienceDaily: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds
data.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has revealed surprising new details about a mysterious, 93-billion-mile-long cloud of dark, fluffy dust that may have formed when massive planetary bodies collided. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about the structure and offers new clues about the violent birth of planetary systems.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds

data.title: ScienceDaily: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
data.summary: Scientists have discovered a remarkably preserved 450-million-year-old fossil containing soft tissues from an ancient starfish relative, revealing unexpected details about marine life more than 200 million years before dinosaurs existed. Found in a museum collection, the extraordinarily rare specimen offers new clues about how Earth's earliest reef animals fed, survived, and evolved.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue

data.title: ScienceDaily: Cancer uses antioxidants to disarm the immune system, scientists discover
data.summary: Scientists have discovered that tumors release natural antioxidants to shut down the immune cells responsible for destroying cancer, exploiting a surprising weakness in the body's defenses. Blocking this mechanism in mice restored immune activity and improved immunotherapy responses, potentially opening a new path toward more effective cancer treatments.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Cancer uses antioxidants to disarm the immune system, scientists discover

data.title: ScienceDaily: Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth
data.summary: A century-old theory about the origins of life on Earth may be wrong. New research from the University of Cambridge suggests that comets traveled too fast and struck at unfavorable angles for the fragile molecules needed for life to survive, making successful delivery extraordinarily unlikely. Surprisingly, Mars may have had a better chance of receiving these cosmic ingredients, although even there the odds were slim. The findings point toward asteroids or chemical processes on Earth as more plausible sources of life's building blocks.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Comets may have destroyed life's ingredients instead of delivering them to Earth

data.title: ScienceDaily: Global fossil fuel emissions set to fall in 2026, but total CO2 keeps rising
data.summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground, but rising emissions from deforestation threaten to push total CO2 emissions to a new record. Scientists warn that the world's remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C could be exhausted in less than four years, even as a lasting decline in emissions appears increasingly within reach.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Global fossil fuel emissions set to fall in 2026, but total CO2 keeps rising

data.title: ScienceDaily: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
data.summary: After more than a year of simulated life on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally emerged from isolation, bringing a remarkable space exploration experiment to an end. Their experiences growing food, conserving resources, and overcoming Mars-like challenges could help NASA prepare for humanity's future on the Moon and Mars.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation

data.title: ScienceDaily: NASA offers $500,000 to develop next-generation electric rocket engines
data.summary: NASA is putting $500,000 on the line in a new competition to accelerate the development of advanced electric rocket engines for satellites and future space exploration. The AMPERE Challenge will reward up to two U.S. companies with cash prizes and access to NASA testing facilities to help bring promising propulsion technology closer to real-world missions.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: NASA offers $500,000 to develop next-generation electric rocket engines

data.title: ScienceDaily: Why heart attacks can still happen even when bad cholesterol is low

data.title: ScienceDaily: Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest
data.summary: A new study found that energy drinks and stimulant supplements were linked to disproportionately frequent reports of serious heart problems, including 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest and 4.5 times more reports of heart attacks. data.title: ScienceDaily: Obesity linked to up to 27% lower risk of death in dementia
data.summary: A surprising study of more than 4,500 older adults found that people who were overweight or obese when diagnosed with dementia had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than those at a normal weight. Researchers suspect that extra energy and muscle reserves may help patients survive the disease's toll on the body, although the reason for the survival advantage remains unclear.

data.title: ScienceDaily: The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved

data.title: ScienceDaily: NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade
data.summary: The Antarctic ozone hole expanded to its seventh-largest size on record in 2026, driven by unusual weather conditions that pushed it close to its historic maximum. Scientists say international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals prevented even greater damage, and Earth's protective ozone layer is still recovering.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts
data.summary: Ancient manuscripts, including the 1,000-year-old York Gospels, have revealed traces of a deadly sheep virus whose history stretches back more than 3,700 years. Scientists discovered that the virus has remained remarkably unchanged for millennia, turning historic parchment into an unexpected record of ancient disease outbreaks.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists uncover a 192-year-old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin
data.summary: A bizarrely deformed 1834 British silver coin found at a car boot sale may preserve evidence of a rare minting accident nearly 200 years ago. Advanced 3D scans and microscopic analysis revealed unusual metal distortions suggesting the coin was crushed under extreme pressure, potentially during its original production.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists uncover a 192-year-old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin

data.title: ScienceDaily: Where are all the males? Ancient human fossils reveal a startling mystery
data.summary: A remarkable discovery in a South African cave suggests that an extinct human relative may have created an all-female burial site more than 240,000 years ago. Scientists analyzed ancient proteins preserved in Homo naledi teeth and found no male-specific markers among at least 20 individuals, potentially solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for over a decade.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Where are all the males? Ancient human fossils reveal a startling mystery

data.title: ScienceDaily: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
data.summary: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior. University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observations, finding that it could explain galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought

data.title: ScienceDaily: Cancer-fighting chewing gum slashes HPV levels by up to 93%
data.summary: A surprising new weapon against microbes linked to head and neck cancer could be as simple as chewing gum. Scientists developed a bioengineered gum that reduced HPV levels by up to 93% in oral samples from cancer patients and nearly eliminated two harmful bacterial species after a single dose of its extract. Even more promising, the treatment spared beneficial bacteria in the mouth.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Cancer-fighting chewing gum slashes HPV levels by up to 93%
